key_leaders: Mahatma Gandhi, Raj Kumar Shukla, Rajendra Prasad, J. B. Kripalani, Mahadev Desai
organizations_involved: Local Ryot assemblies and early Gandhian volunteer teams
triggering_events: European planters imposing the Tinkathia system (compulsory cultivation of indigo on 3/20th of tenant land) and imposing illegal rent exactions
core_objectives: Abolition of the Tinkathia system, refund of illegally collected exactions (Tawan/Sharbeshi), and freedom for tenants to cultivate chosen crops
methods_and_activities: Systematic on-site testimony collection, defiance of administrative expulsion orders, refusal to pay bail, and strictly non-violent resistance
british_reaction: Lt. Governor of Bihar ordered withdrawal of cases against Gandhi and constituted the Champaran Agrarian Inquiry Committee with Gandhi as a member
withdrawal_or_outcome: Passage of the Champaran Agrarian Act of 1918, which abolished the Tinkathia system and secured a 25% refund of illegal exactions
historical_significance: Gandhi's first experiment with civil disobedience on Indian soil, validating Satyagraha as an effective weapon of mass protest

key_leaders: Mahatma Gandhi, Motilal Nehru, C. R. Das, Lala Lajpat Rai, Rajendra Prasad, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
organizations_involved: Indian National Congress (Nagpur session 1920 structural reorganization), All India Khilafat Committee
triggering_events: Jallianwala Bagh Massacre, Hunter Committee findings, Rowlatt Act detentions, and the dismemberment of the Ottoman Caliphate (Khilafat grievance)
core_objectives: Redressal of the Punjab and Khilafat wrongs, and the attainment of Swaraj through peaceful and legitimate non-cooperation
methods_and_activities: Surrender of British titles, boycott of government schools, civil courts, legislative councils, and imported textiles; picketing of liquor stores; promotion of Charkha and Khadi
geographical_spread: Pan-India (United Provinces, Bengal, Bombay Presidency, Bihar, Madras Presidency, Punjab, Assam)
mass_participation: Urban middle classes, students, lawyers, peasant tenants, women, and workers across religious communities
british_reaction: Declaration of Congress Volunteer Corps as unlawful, mass arrests of over 30,000 activists, and banning of assemblies
withdrawal_or_outcome: Halted by Gandhi following the violent Chauri Chaura incident in Gorakhpur on February 4–5, 1922, where 22 policemen were killed
historical_significance: Transformed the Indian freedom struggle from an elite constitutional reform movement into a nationwide mass anti-colonial struggle

key_leaders: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Kalyanji Mehta, Mithubehn Petit, Bhaktiba Desai
organizations_involved: Bardoli Taluka Congress Committee, local Chhavanis (worker camps)
triggering_events: Arbitrary 22% (initially 30%) enhancement of land revenue rates imposed by the Bombay Presidency Government despite falling agricultural commodity prices
core_objectives: Total revocation of the enhanced land assessment and appointment of an independent judicial inquiry
methods_and_activities: Pledge to refuse revenue payment, total non-cooperation, social boycotts of revenue bailiffs, and mobilization of women volunteers
mass_participation: Complete unity of Kunbi-Patidar peasants, Kaliparaj (adivasi) agricultural laborers, and women satyagrahis
british_reaction: Confiscation and auction of ancestral lands and cattle; deployment of outside bailiffs to intimidate villagers, which failed
withdrawal_or_outcome: Government conceded; Maxwell-Broomfield Commission reduced the revenue increase to 6.03% and restored all seized lands
historical_significance: Vallabhbhai Patel was conferred the title of 'Sardar' by the women of Bardoli; served as the operational model for the 1930 Civil Disobedience Movement

key_leaders: Mahatma Gandhi, Sarojini Naidu, C. Rajagopalachari, Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, K. Kelappan
organizations_involved: Indian National Congress, Khudai Khidmatgars, Sabarmati Ashram volunteers
triggering_events: Viceroy Irwin's rejection of Gandhi's Eleven Demands; state monopoly and oppressive taxation on salt, an essential commodity
core_objectives: Defiance of colonial salt laws, non-payment of land and chowkidari taxes, and achievement of Purna Swaraj (Complete Independence)
methods_and_activities: 240-mile Dandi March, manufacturing illicit salt on open shores, non-payment of taxes, picketing of foreign cloth and liquor, defying forest laws
geographical_spread: Sabarmati to Dandi (Gujarat), Vedaranyam (Tamil Nadu), Payyanur (Kerala), Peshawar (NWFP), Dharasana, and Midnapore
mass_participation: Mass mobilization across classes: peasants refusing rent, merchant guilds halting trade, women picketing shops, and tribal groups defying forest acts
british_reaction: Arrest of over 90,000 participants including Gandhi and Nehru, declaration of the INC as unlawful, and severe police lathi charges
withdrawal_or_outcome: Suspended on March 5, 1931, with the signing of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact, enabling Congress participation in the Second Round Table Conference
historical_significance: A major demonstration of mass civil disobedience that shook the moral authority of the British Empire in India and engaged the British government on equal negotiating terms

key_leaders: Mahatma Gandhi, Aruna Asaf Ali, Jayaprakash Narayan, Ram Manohar Lohia, Usha Mehta, Nana Patil, Chittu Pandey
organizations_involved: Indian National Congress, Congress Socialist Party (CSP), local underground revolutionary action committees
triggering_events: Failure of the Cripps Mission, imminent threat of Japanese invasion, wartime economic inflation, and acute food shortages
core_objectives: Immediate and unconditional end of British colonial rule from Indian soil, centered on Gandhi's call: 'Do or Die'
methods_and_activities: Attacks on communication infrastructure, burning of railway stations, hoisting tricolor flags on public offices, underground radio broadcasting, and setting up parallel governments (Prati Sarkars)
geographical_spread: Pan-India (major strongholds in Ballia, Midnapore, Satara, Talcher, Bihar, Bombay)
mass_participation: Spontaneous mass uprising of peasants, industrial factory workers, students, underground socialists, and government employees
british_reaction: Severe state repression, strafing of crowds from military airplanes, collective punitive fines, and imprisonment of over 100,000 activists
withdrawal_or_outcome: Violently suppressed within months, but parallel local administrations (e.g., Satara) persisted underground through 1944–1945
historical_significance: Demonstrated that British rule had lost legitimacy and made clear that post-war transfer of sovereign power was inevitable
